media.caption: The Tlajinga project describes obsidian production in Compound 17 and shared courtyards and drains in the investigated compounds. This original guide connects activities and spaces without copying a source plan. The connecting line is a teaching relationship, not a street, an artifact route or a claim that every task occurred simultaneously.

media.caption: Figure 1 combines the Teotihuacan Mapping Project base with later PATT and Widmer/Storey fieldwork. Upper panel: city reference with north arrow and 1 km scale. Lower panel: southern Tlajinga, San Lorenzo River, Street of the Dead, Compounds 17, 18 and 33, and the platform group, with a 200 m scale. This is a composite locator map, not a single-phase household plan. Its small original labels need enlargement; the readable text here retains the key spatial relationships. No numerical compound coordinates or political boundary are inferred.
notice: Find Tlajinga (7) in the upper city map, then Compounds 17 and 18 in the lower detail.
